in running status, so "all 16 voices struck again every block"
      can't arrive by MIDI. The test (mididense) and the loaded measure
      fill the wire instead (all 16 voices sounding, notes struck again
      continuously); a faster input (USB MIDI, M11) could come closer.
  - **Next: M6b, MIDI out**, waiting on the spec side (which port the FM-1
    sends MIDI on; the spec side has #82 open on MIDI output).

### M6b: MIDI out (firmware side)
- Status 2026-10-24 (session M6b, firmware side, on the owner's Mac): done,
  in pull requests #90 (start) and the MIDI out pull request (the sender,
  what the panel sends, thru, local control, the settings on the screen,
  the tests), which needs fwtest 0.5.0's pin (#91) on main first.
  - **The sender** (HW-72 to HW-74): a 32-message queue that only the
    engine's block callback writes and drains; UART1's transmit DMA,
    started only when the last transfer has gone (`CON0` bit 15), whole
    messages up to 12 bytes a transfer; no interrupt, no lock, nothing
    waits for the wire. Running status while messages keep coming; the
    first message after the wire goes quiet carries its status.
  - **The policy:** controllers, bends, pressure and program changes merge
    with a waiting one; 8 places kept for note offs; others dropped and
    counted when full; a note on dropped takes its note off with it; a
    note off that finds the queue full drops the newest message that ends
    no notes. Nothing is left on at the far end.
  - **What is sent**, on the out channel (1): the keys (velocity 100, the
    off as velocity 0), KNOB1 to KNOB4 as controllers 16 to 19 (the
    inverse of M6a's map, when the value changes), PRESETS as program
    changes, SEL with MONO or POLY as the mode messages. The panel has no
    other pitch control.
  - **Thru** (off by default) passes on every message received but SysEx,
    before the channel filter; **local control** (on by default, CC 122
    too) off sends the panel to MIDI out only. The settings are in
    `struct midi_settings` version 2 and on the screen's bottom line.
  - **Tests** (fwtest 0.5.0, `--midi-out`): six cases, R-MIDIOUT-1 to
    R-MIDIOUT-8. midiout's 60 messages exactly as its script implies
    (golden); the round trip (midiout's golden capture into MIDI in) ends
    with the same patch, mode and knobs and the same pitches; thru passes
    on 18 messages in order and the panel's 4 once each (golden); local
    control off plays nothing from the panel (golden screen); a burst of
    94 messages in one block: 28 merged, 18 dropped with 16 note offs, none
    lost, every note sent ended, the panel's keys out again after (golden);
    the wire's timing and one run per transfer in every case.
  - **Figures** (fwtest 0.5.0): latency from a key going down to its note
    on's first start bit 3.26 to 5.29 ms (mean 4.20; debounce, then at most
    a block); the wire carries about 88% of its rate under a stream (a
    transfer starts only at a poll). At rest 1 863.9 instructions a block,
    +25 (+1.4%); loaded 110 207.6, +0.3%; code 20 144 bytes (+1 736),
    static RAM 143 776 (+520): the M6 budgets hold, none raised. audiogold
    and fmgold unchanged; chords' and midipanel's screens moved only by
    the settings line.
  - **Open items:**
    - **The transmitter on the chip.** Which pin, if any, carries UART1's
      transmit side on the FM-1 is open (Q-20); the FM-1 has no MIDI OUT
      jack, so on the device the bytes go nowhere; in the app they reach
      other programs. What a `CON0` write during a transfer does on the
      chip, beyond the acknowledge, is not known.
    - **Throughput:** with polling once or twice a block, a full input
      wire passed on by thru is about 12% more than the out wire carries;
      the policy then merges or drops. A transmit interrupt (its enable is
      known only from the emulator) would close the gap.
    - **No UI for the settings yet:** they are set by test builds and CC
      122; M8's UI changes them, M7 saves them.
  - **Next: M7, flash storage.**

### M1 to M9 (firmware side)
- **M1** boot: clocks, interrupts, timer (done; above).
- **M2** screen (done; above).
- **M3** keys, encoders, pot, LEDs (done; above).
- **M4** audio (done; above). **M4b** a platform test: Plaits (MIT) as
  a demo build, and the loaded-case budget (done; above).
- **M5** the FM engine (done; above).
- **M6a** MIDI in (done; above). **M6b** MIDI out (done; above).
- **M7** flash storage (next).
- **M8** UI and original presets (no Yamaha factory voices).
- **M9** packaging, and a raw-image boot path in the app.

### Level 2: real hardware
- **M10** recovery kit.
- **M11** USB-MIDI and the update handler.
- **M12** hardware checklist.

## Risks

- **The toolchain's availability and terms.** JieLi's Linux toolchain has no
  licence file (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md). We never redistribute it. If the
  download disappears, a full rebuild needs another copy (the private
  preservation repo), but every released binary stays verifiable by its
  recorded hash. The vendor's short link already points at a newer release
  (20260730.1) than the pinned one; the pinned file is fetched by its direct
  URL.
- **Packages for real hardware.** A `.fwsc` package may need M-VAVE's boot or
  update loader, which we can't redistribute. Find out from FM-1-RE's
  documents only, before M9, and record the answer here. The app is
  unaffected (it can boot our raw image). *Answer, in part (2026-10-24,
  session midi-in-out, from FM1 Open's terms only; docs/EXPOSURE.md):*
  M-VAVE now distributes its boot and update resources (`uboot.boot`,
  `ota.bin`, `cfg_tool.bin`, `boot-config.bin`) and the FM-1's recovery
  image (`FM-1_015.fwsc`) under Apache-2.0, which allows redistribution,
  binary included, with the licence, the notices and modified files
  marked. So the loader is no longer a licence obstacle; whether a package
  of ours needs it is still to find out from FM-1-RE's documents. The
  recovery image is still M-VAVE's stock firmware: clean sessions never
  open or disassemble it (CONTRIBUTING.md), whatever its licence.
- **FM1 Open's terms** (M-VAVE's `m-vave/fm1_open`, read 2026-10-24: its
  `LICENSE.md` and `THIRD_PARTY.md` only, at
  `4c7496daac04a95ff10d1afdcc8f9ead2dbabc41`; never its code). It is a GPL
  firmware, so it stays forbidden to the firmware side and outside the
  spec side's allowed sources. What the terms allow, for the record:
  - its own app sources: GPLv3 only, with an additional permission under
    GPLv3 section 7 to link with M-VAVE's binary SDK and convey the result
    without that SDK's source (the third party's summary, "GPLv3 with a
    linking exception plus a proprietary binary SDK", is right; it is
    GPLv3 *only*, not "or later");
  - the binary engine library: proprietary, no source; anyone
    may copy it, link it, build, install and run the result, and
    redistribute it in binary form, commercially too, but only for
    M-VAVE FM1 devices, with the notices and `THIRD_PARTY.md`;
  - the boot and update resources and the recovery image: Apache-2.0
    (above); the third-party parts (FreeRTOS, micro-ecc, Newlib,
    compiler-rt, MSFA and Dexed, Open303, DaisySP, stmlib, emu2149, the SEA
    codec, the packager) and JieLi's SDK material keep their own licences;
  - flashing: the terms permit installing and running such firmware on FM1
    devices, warn that defects may lose data or make the device
    malfunction, and disclaim warranty for the app and the binary SDK.
  For us: our firmware links nothing of FM1 Open, so none of its
  conditions applies to our code; the engine grant names FM1 devices only,
  so it would not cover the SMK-37.
- **The emulator doesn't model USB**, so M11 is hardware-only.
- **Merge signatures are GitHub's.** Since 2026-10-22 the owner merges with
  GitHub's button, so merge commits are signed by GitHub (`web-flow`) and the
  owner's identity rests on GitHub's `merged_by` record, checked by C-MERGE.
  Milestone tags carry the owner's own SSH signature. The first merge's
  record shows C-MERGE FAIL under the earlier rule (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge
  policy and its history").

    (golden); the round trip (midiout's golden capture into MIDI in) ends
    with the same patch, mode and knobs and the same pitches; thru passes
    on 18 messages in order and the panel's 4 once each (golden); local
    control off plays nothing from the panel (golden screen); a burst of
    94 messages in one block: 28 merged, 18 dropped with 16 note offs, none
    lost, every note sent ended, the panel's keys out again after (golden);
    the wire's timing and one run per transfer in every case.
  - **Figures** (fwtest 0.5.0): latency from a key going down to its note
    on's first start bit 3.26 to 5.29 ms (mean 4.20; debounce, then at most
    a block); the wire carries about 88% of its rate under a stream (a
    transfer starts only at a poll). At rest 1 863.9 instructions a block,
    +25 (+1.4%); loaded 110 207.6, +0.3%; code 20 144 bytes (+1 736),
    static RAM 143 776 (+520): the M6 budgets hold, none raised. audiogold
    and fmgold unchanged; chords' and midipanel's screens moved only by
    the settings line.
  - **Open items:**
    - **The transmitter on the chip.** Which pin, if any, carries UART1's
      transmit side on the FM-1 is open (Q-20); the FM-1 has no MIDI OUT
      jack, so on the device the bytes go nowhere; in the app they reach
      other programs. What a `CON0` write during a transfer does on the
      chip, beyond the acknowledge, is not known.
    - **Throughput:** with polling once or twice a block, a full input
      wire passed on by thru is about 12% more than the out wire carries;
      the policy then merges or drops. A transmit interrupt (its enable is
      known only from the emulator) would close the gap.
    - **No UI for the settings yet:** they are set by test builds and CC
      122; M8's UI changes them, M7 saves them.
  - **Next: M7, flash storage.**

- **M1** boot: clocks, interrupts, timer (done; above).
- **M2** screen (done; above).
- **M3** keys, encoders, pot, LEDs (done; above).
- **M4** audio (done; above). **M4b** a platform test: Plaits (MIT) as
  a demo build, and the loaded-case budget (done; above).
- **M5** the FM engine (done; above).
- **M6a** MIDI in (done; above). **M6b** MIDI out (done; above).
- **M7** flash storage (next).
- **M8** UI and original presets (no Yamaha factory voices).
- **M9** packaging, and a raw-image boot path in the app.

### Level 2: real hardware
- **M10** recovery kit.
- **M11** USB-MIDI and the update handler.
- **M12** hardware checklist.

## Risks

- **The toolchain's availability and terms.** JieLi's Linux toolchain has no
  licence file (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md). We never redistribute it. If the
  download disappears, a full rebuild needs another copy (the private
  preservation repo), but every released binary stays verifiable by its
  recorded hash. The vendor's short link already points at a newer release
  (20260730.1) than the pinned one; the pinned file is fetched by its direct
  URL.
- **Packages for real hardware.** A `.fwsc` package may need M-VAVE's boot or
  update loader, which we can't redistribute. Find out from FM-1-RE's
  documents only, before M9, and record the answer here. The app is
  unaffected (it can boot our raw image). *Answer, in part (2026-10-24,
  session midi-in-out, from FM1 Open's terms only; docs/EXPOSURE.md):*
  M-VAVE now distributes its boot and update resources (`uboot.boot`,
  `ota.bin`, `cfg_tool.bin`, `boot-config.bin`) and the FM-1's recovery
  image (`FM-1_015.fwsc`) under Apache-2.0, which allows redistribution,
  binary included, with the licence, the notices and modified files
  marked. So the loader is no longer a licence obstacle; whether a package
  of ours needs it is still to find out from FM-1-RE's documents. The
  recovery image is still M-VAVE's stock firmware: clean sessions never
  open or disassemble it (CONTRIBUTING.md), whatever its licence.
- **FM1 Open's terms** (M-VAVE's `m-vave/fm1_open`, read 2026-10-24: its
  `LICENSE.md` and `THIRD_PARTY.md` only, at
  `4c7496daac04a95ff10d1afdcc8f9ead2dbabc41`; never its code). It is a GPL
  firmware, so it stays forbidden to the firmware side and outside the
  spec side's allowed sources. What the terms allow, for the record:
  - its own app sources: GPLv3 only, with an additional permission under
    GPLv3 section 7 to link with M-VAVE's binary SDK and convey the result
    without that SDK's source (the third party's summary, "GPLv3 with a
    linking exception plus a proprietary binary SDK", is right; it is
    GPLv3 *only*, not "or later");
  - the binary engine library: proprietary, no source; anyone
    may copy it, link it, build, install and run the result, and
    redistribute it in binary form, commercially too, but only for
    M-VAVE FM1 devices, with the notices and `THIRD_PARTY.md`;
  - the boot and update resources and the recovery image: Apache-2.0
    (above); the third-party parts (FreeRTOS, micro-ecc, Newlib,
    compiler-rt, MSFA and Dexed, Open303, DaisySP, stmlib, emu2149, the SEA
    codec, the packager) and JieLi's SDK material keep their own licences;
  - flashing: the terms permit installing and running such firmware on FM1
    devices, warn that defects may lose data or make the device
    malfunction, and disclaim warranty for the app and the binary SDK.
  For us: our firmware links nothing of FM1 Open, so none of its
  conditions applies to our code; the engine grant names FM1 devices only,
  so it would not cover the SMK-37.
- **The emulator doesn't model USB**, so M11 is hardware-only.
- **Merge signatures are GitHub's.** Since 2026-10-22 the owner merges with
  GitHub's button, so merge commits are signed by GitHub (`web-flow`) and the
  owner's identity rests on GitHub's `merged_by` record, checked by C-MERGE.
  Milestone tags carry the owner's own SSH signature. The first merge's
  record shows C-MERGE FAIL under the earlier rule (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge
  policy and its history").

# The FM engine's patch format, version 1

A patch is everything the FM engine (M5, `firmware/src/fm.h`) needs to
play a sound: 112 bytes, each field one byte, or two bytes little-endian,
so a patch can be saved to flash (M7) and shared (the app) as it is,
without conversion. `tools/fm_patch.py` writes and checks patches in this
format (its `encode` and `problems`), and `fm_patch_valid()` in
`firmware/src/fm_play.c` checks them the same way. The test patches are
defined once, in `tools/fm_patch.py`, and generated into
`firmware/src/patches.c`; they are our own (R-FM-7).

## Layout

| Offset | Bytes | Field | Values |
|-------:|------:|-------|--------|
| 0 | 2 | magic | `F` `M` (0x46, 0x4D) |
| 2 | 1 | version | 1 |
| 3 | 1 | length | 112, the whole patch |
| 4 | 12 | name | printable ASCII (32 to 126), padded with 0 |
| 16 | 1 | algorithm | 1 to 10 ("The algorithms", docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M5) |
| 17 | 1 | feedback | 0 (none) to 7, on the algorithm's feedback operator |
| 18 | 1 | flags | bit 0: mono; the other bits 0 |
| 19 | 1 | glide | a time code (below); 0: none. Mono only |
| 20 | 1 | transpose | signed semitones, -24 to 24 |
| 21 | 1 | pitch depth | signed semitones that a pitch level of 127 means, -48 to 48 |
| 22 | 3 | pitch rates | time codes: P0 to P1, P1 to P2 (then held), and to P3 on release |
| 25 | 4 | pitch levels | P0 (at note on) to P3, signed, -127 to 127 |
| 29 | 3 | reserved | 0 |
| 32 | 6 x 13 | operators | operator 1 first (below) |
| 110 | 2 | check sum | Fletcher-16 of bytes 0 to 109: low byte the first sum, high byte the second, each mod 255 |

Each operator, 13 bytes from its first:

| Offset | Bytes | Field | Values |
|-------:|------:|-------|--------|
| 0 | 1 | mode | 0: a ratio of the note's frequency; 1: a fixed frequency |
| 1 | 2 | frequency | ratio x 256 (256 is 1.0, up to 255.996), or a fixed frequency in quarter hertz |
| 3 | 1 | detune | signed cents, -100 to 100 |
| 4 | 1 | level | 0 (off) to 127; gain 2^((level - 127) / 8) |
| 5 | 1 | velocity | sensitivity 0 to 7: at 7, velocity 0 is 8 octaves (48.2 dB) quieter than 127, in proportion between |
| 6 | 4 | rates | time codes: attack, decay 1, decay 2, release |
| 10 | 3 | levels | 0 to 127, as level: the attack's peak, the level after decay 1, the level held |

## Units

- **A time code** t, 0 to 127, is 2^(t / 8) ms, from 1 ms to 60.1 s: the
  time a stage takes over its whole range. The attack's range is a gain
  of 0 to 1; the decays' and the release's is 16 octaves (96.3 dB); the
  pitch envelope's 254 levels. A stage that moves only part of its range
  takes that part of the time.
- **A level** step is 2^(1/8), 0.753 dB; 127 is 0 dB.
- **An operator's index**: a modulator at full level moves its carrier's
  phase by 4 pi radians at the most (fm.c, `MOD_SHIFT`); level 103 (a gain
  of 1/8) is index pi/2.
- **Feedback** k (1 to 7) moves the operator's phase by up to
  pi / 2^(7 - k) times the mean of its last two outputs.

## Versions

Version 1 is the first (M5). A reader must refuse a patch with another
magic, version or length, a bad check sum or a field out of range: it
never guesses. A later version will keep the first four bytes' meaning,
so any reader can tell a patch it doesn't know from a damaged one, and
will say here what changed.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

#
# The firmware's fwtest suite (docs/HARNESS.md, "Suites"). tools/fw-suite.py
# puts the image under test at out/fw/app.bin and the test images (the same
# source built with one SB_TEST_* define each) beside it, runs this suite

MIDI_CHECKS = {"midimsg": check_midimsg, "midirun": midi_only("midirun"),
               "midisysex": midi_only("midisysex"), "midijunk": midi_only("midijunk", last_only=True),
               "mididense": check_mididense, "midisustain": check_midisustain,
               "midichan": check_midichan, "midipanel": check_midipanel, "midilat": check_midilat,
               "midiout": check_midiout, "midiround": check_midiround, "midithru": check_midithru,
               "midilocal": check_midilocal, "midiburst": check_midiburst, "midioutlat": check_midioutlat}


AUDIO_CHECKS = {"tone": check_tone, "notes": check_notes, "audioload": check_audioload,
                "audiogold": check_audiogold, "underrun": check_underrun,
                "fmbessel": check_fmbessel, "fmenv": check_fmenv, "fmmono": check_fmmono,
                "fmsteal": check_fmsteal, "fmvel": check_fmvel, "fmgold": check_fmgold, "fmgold2": check_fmgold}
AUDIO_CHECKS.update(MIDI_CHECKS)


INPUT_CHECKS = {"keys": check_keys, "chords": check_chords, "encoders": check_encoders, "pot": check_pot,
                "leds": check_leds, "ledshow": check_ledshow}


def build_tests(build):
    """Builds the test images; returns problems."""
    problems = []
    for name, define in sorted(TEST_BUILDS.items()):
        out = os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", "build-" + name)
        p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", out, "--define", define],
                           cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            problems.append("%s: the build failed:\n%s" % (name, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-2000:]))
            continue
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(out, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", name + ".bin"))
        print("built %s (-D%s)" % (name, define))
    return problems


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    global START_SLACK
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            sizes = dict(l.split() for l in f if l.strip())
        print("image size: " + ", ".join("%s %s" % kv for kv in sizes.items()))
        START_SLACK = start_slack(int(sizes.get("bss", 0)))
        print("start slack: %d time base ticks (bss cleared before main starts the time base)" % START_SLACK)
    symbols = elf_symbols(os.path.join(a.build, "app.elf"))
    problems = build_tests(a.build)

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    if p.returncode != 0:
        problems.append("fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode)

    steady = {}
    for name in EXPECT:
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        for g in result.get("golden") or []:
            print("  golden %s: %s" % (g.get("name"), g.get("result")))
            if g.get("result") != "match":
                problems.append("%s: golden %s: %s" % (name, g.get("name"), g.get("detail")))
        if name in ("boot", "screen", "fault", "stray", "chords") and not result.get("golden"):
            problems.append("%s: no golden files compared" % name)
        case_dir = os.path.join(out, name)
        more, lines = [], []
        if name == "boot":
            more, lines = check_boot(case_dir, symbols)
        elif name in ("heartbeat", "heartbeat2") and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(case_dir, result)
            with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
                steady[name] = (result, beacon(f.read()))
            if len(steady) == 2:
                m, l = check_steady([steady["heartbeat"][0], steady["heartbeat2"][0]],
                                    [steady["heartbeat"][1], steady["heartbeat2"][1]])
                more, lines = more + m, lines + l
        elif name == "screen":
            more, lines = check_screen(case_dir)
        elif name == "flood" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_flood(case_dir, result, os.path.join(out, "screen"))
        elif name == "fault":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STACK, 1)
        elif name == "stray":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STRAY, 127)
        elif name in INPUT_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            more, lines = INPUT_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
        elif name in AUDIO_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            try:
                more, lines = AUDIO_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
                more, lines = ["%s: %s" % (name, e)], []
        problems += more
        if lines:
            print("\n".join(lines))

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def build_tests(build):
    """Builds the test images; returns problems."""
    problems = []
    for name, define in sorted(TEST_BUILDS.items()):
        out = os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", "build-" + name)
        p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", out, "--define", define],
                           cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            problems.append("%s: the build failed:\n%s" % (name, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-2000:]))
            continue
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(out, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", name + ".bin"))
        print("built %s (-D%s)" % (name, define))
    return problems


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    global START_SLACK
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            sizes = dict(l.split() for l in f if l.strip())
        print("image size: " + ", ".join("%s %s" % kv for kv in sizes.items()))
        START_SLACK = start_slack(int(sizes.get("bss", 0)))
        print("start slack: %d time base ticks (bss cleared before main starts the time base)" % START_SLACK)
    symbols = elf_symbols(os.path.join(a.build, "app.elf"))
    problems = build_tests(a.build)

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    if p.returncode != 0:
        problems.append("fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode)

    steady = {}
    for name in EXPECT:
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        for g in result.get("golden") or []:
            print("  golden %s: %s" % (g.get("name"), g.get("result")))
            if g.get("result") != "match":
                problems.append("%s: golden %s: %s" % (name, g.get("name"), g.get("detail")))
        if name in ("boot", "screen", "fault", "stray", "chords") and not result.get("golden"):
            problems.append("%s: no golden files compared" % name)
        case_dir = os.path.join(out, name)
        more, lines = [], []
        if name == "boot":
            more, lines = check_boot(case_dir, symbols)
        elif name in ("heartbeat", "heartbeat2") and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(case_dir, result)
            with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
                steady[name] = (result, beacon(f.read()))
            if len(steady) == 2:
                m, l = check_steady([steady["heartbeat"][0], steady["heartbeat2"][0]],
                                    [steady["heartbeat"][1], steady["heartbeat2"][1]])
                more, lines = more + m, lines + l
        elif name == "screen":
            more, lines = check_screen(case_dir)
        elif name == "flood" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_flood(case_dir, result, os.path.join(out, "screen"))
        elif name == "fault":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STACK, 1)
        elif name == "stray":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STRAY, 127)
        elif name in INPUT_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            more, lines = INPUT_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
        elif name in AUDIO_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            try:
                more, lines = AUDIO_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
                more, lines = ["%s: %s" % (name, e)], []
        problems += more
        if lines:
            print("\n".join(lines))

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

/*

 *
 * The input layer: every control on the panel, and its LEDs (M3). This is
 * the API the rest of the firmware, and engines built on it, use; keep it
 * small and stable (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M3, "The input API").
 *
 * - One event queue, read with input_read(). Each event names a control,
 *   what happened to it, a value and the time it was decided.
 * - Control IDs are named after the panel's printed labels (HW-36). Their
 *   numbers never change; a board wired differently from fwtest (Q-7)
 *   changes only input.c's tables.
 * - input_value() gives a control's present state at any time.
 * - input_led() sets the LED of a button or key, with a brightness.
 * - Since M4, input_read_audio() hands the same events to the audio
 *   engine, from a queue of its own (audio.h).
 */

#define INPUT_H

#include "sb.h"

#define INPUT_SAVE       9u
#define INPUT_ARP        10u
#define INPUT_SEQ        11u
#define INPUT_PLAY       12u  /* PLAY/STOP, one button */
#define INPUT_REC        13u

#define INPUT_KEY_GLO    INPUT_KEY(18)
#define INPUT_KEY_MONO   INPUT_KEY(21)
#define INPUT_KEY_POLY   INPUT_KEY(23)
/* Knobs: MASTER is a pot, the other seven are encoders with detents. */
#define INPUT_MASTER     41u
#define INPUT_SELECT     42u
#define INPUT_PRESETS    43u
#define INPUT_ALGORITHM  44u
#define INPUT_KNOB1      45u
#define INPUT_KNOB2      46u
#define INPUT_KNOB3      47u
#define INPUT_KNOB4      48u
#define INPUT_CONTROLS   49u
#define INPUT_LEDS       41u  /* controls 0 to 40 have an LED */

/* What happened (input_event.kind), and its value. */
#define INPUT_PRESS      1u   /* a button or key went down; value 1 */

1	# 09 — Storage: NOR flash driver, norfs/FAT filesystems, VM key-value store, DX7 patches, firmware update
2	
3	Target: M-Vave FM-1, JieLi AC791N/WL82. One external SPI NOR flash holds everything:
4	the firmware XIP image, a small NOR-resident file area ("sdfile"/norfs), a FAT/exFAT
5	volume, the VM (virtual-memory EEPROM-emulation) key-value area used by syscfg, and the
6	raw DX7 bank/patch region. Confidence: **high** = proven, **med** = strong inference,
7	**low** = guess.
8	
9	Primary evidence: `analysis/shards/shard_020847aa_020847f2.txt`,
10	`shard_02084824_0208c3b4.txt` (SPI0/flash low level),
11	`shard_02002154_02003b52.txt` (ROM-call read/write cores),
12	`shard_02027346_02028fc6.txt` (flash ioctl, device framework, update file open),
13	`shard_02028fd2_0202b3d6.txt` + `shard_0202b498_0202e0fa.txt` + `shard_0202e108_0203091c.txt`
14	(FAT/VFS), `shard_02030942_02033964.txt` (VM KV), `shard_02019e9e_0201f07e.txt`
15	(DX7 pack/store), `shard_02082d14_0208478a.txt` (ufw/jlfs).
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 1. NOR flash driver (SPI0)
20	
21	**SPI0 base `0x11C00`** (jielie `spi.md`: CON+0, BUF+8; CON bit15 PND, bit14 PCLR).
22	Low-level (all high conf):
23	
24	| addr | name | notes |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| `0x020847AA` | `spi0_wait_ok` | poll `[0x11C00]` sign bit (PND) with 50 000 000-iteration timeout, clear via `\|= 0x4000`; returns 0 ok / −1 timeout |
27	| `0x020847DA` | `spi0_send_byte` | set TX direction (`\|= 8`, clear bit 12), `[0x11C00+8] = byte`, wait, restore |
28	| `0x0208478A` | `norflash_cs` | CS low/high helper (r0 = 0/1) |
29	| `0x02084700` | `norflash_spi0_guard` | wait SFC idle, save/restore SPI0 CON around bit-banged phases |
30	| `0x020847F2` | `norflash_enter_4byte_addr` | if flash size `[0x1C20190+24] > 16 MB` and addr ≥ 16 MB: one-shot **EN4B `0xB7`** |
31	
32	**Command-mode engine `norflash_cs_and_erase` `0x02084BBE`** (med): enters SFC command
33	mode via SFR **`0x40200`** — saves `[0x1C20190+56]`, programs SPI0 CON from
34	`[0x1C20190+60]`, sets `[0x5101C] |= 0x20`, waits `0x40200` sign bit clear, issues the
35	command. The merged cluster around it contains:
36	
37	- **page program**: WREN (`0x02084824` + verify `0x02084862`), opcode `0x02`,
38	  3/4-byte address via `spiflash_send_addr` `0x02084872`, byte loop, wait-ready
39	  `0x020848D0`, icache sync `0x02084B88` — at `0x02084C24`;
40	- **read**: dispatch `spiflash_io_dispatch` `0x02084A30` (single/dual/quad by chip type);
41	- **erase** at `0x02084D4E`: selector − 200 → `tbb` table —
42	  4 kB sector (`0x20`), 64 kB block (`0xD8`), whole chip (`0xC7`), 256-byte page
43	  (`0x81`, **med**); bounds-checked against `[0x1C20190+24]` flash size;
44	- **JEDEC ID** `0x9F` → 3 bytes into `[0x1C20190+28]`; **unique ID** `0x4B`
45	  (4 dummy + 16 UID bytes) — at `0x02084CC6`.
46	
47	**Normal (memory-mapped) data path** — the CPU reads flash XIP, writes/erases go
48	through mask-ROM services (high):
49	
50	| addr | name | notes |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| `0x0200372C` | `norflash_read_core` | mutex `0x1C0E670+2196` (`os_mutex_pend` `0x0205AE98`), bounds vs `[0x1C20190+24]`, reads in ≤256 B chunks via ROM **`0xFFC00404`** |
53	| `0x020037B4` | `norflash_read` | public wrapper, returns 0 on short read |
54	| `0x0200380A` | `norflash_write_core` | ROM **`0xFFC00476`**; then re-scrambles any data in the encrypted region (`< [0x1C20190+36]`) with the boot key `h[0x1C7FD50+28]` via the LFSR cipher `0x020037C8` |
55	| `0x020038A2` | `norflash_write` | public wrapper, 0 on failure |
56	| `0x02001D33A` | `norflash_ioctl` | device ioctl: erase/write/cache-control commands, mutex-guarded (cmd 206 = query VM area, used by `vm_area_init`) |
57	| `0x02028BA2` | `norflash_dev_init` | JEDEC read, capacity = 2^n, registers the device into the framework |
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 2. Filesystems
62	
63	Two stacks share the flash through the device framework (devices `'norflash'`
64	`0x02055780`, `'nor_sdfile'` `0x0205572D`, `'sdfile_fat'` `0x02055738`, `'ramfs'`
65	`0x0204EAEC`, `'virtual'` `0x0204EC40`).
66	
67	### 2.1 norfs — the "sdfile" NOR area (med)
68	
69	A tiny JieLi filesystem of **CRC'd 32-byte directory entries** directly on NOR flash:
70	
71	- `norfs_fopen` `0x020286A0` — resolve path → 40 B file object (`norfs_file_obj_init`
72	  `0x02028220`), trailing read/write/seek/close ops;
73	- `norfs_path_find` `0x0202852C`, `norfs_dir_find_entry` `0x020283D0`,
74	  `norfs_entry_scan` `0x0202847A` (≤32 entries, crc16 + name match),
75	  `norfs_addr_remap` `0x020283B4`;
76	- FM-1 content: `mnt/sdfile/app/usr` `0x0204F0A1`, `mnt/sdfile/app/btif` `0x0204F12E`,
77	  `mnt/sdfile/app/cfg_tool.bin` `0x0204F33C`, `res.bin` `0x0204EC48` (UI resources,
78	  read through `ui_res_read` `0x020100CE` with read-ahead cache).
79	
80	### 2.2 FAT12/16/32 + exFAT (FatFS-derived, extended)
81	
82	| addr | name | notes | conf |
83	|---|---|---|---|
84	| `0x02029352` | `mount_volume` | parse BPB; exFAT detected via OEM field at +67 (`u32` + `'T'` byte check, `0x02029374..0x0202939C`); FAT12/16/32 by cluster count | high |
85	| `0x02029210` | `mount_alloc_fs` | allocate + link FATFS object, query sector count | med |
86	| `0x0202AEF8` | `fatfs_obj_alloc` | 812-byte filesystem work object | low |
87	| `0x020292FC` | `move_window` | sync then load sector into the FAT window | high |
88	| `0x0202C19A` | `fatfs_open` | open/create by path, truncate + exFAT handling | med |
89	| `0x0202CA26` | `fatfs_fopen` | mode-string (`r`/`w`/`rb`) front-end | med |
90	| `0x02029762` | `f_mkfs` | format: pick geometry, write BPB/FAT/root | high |
91	| `0x0202E1E2` | `fat_dir_walk` | recursive walk: attr filter, wildcard, callback, path stack | med |
92	| `0x0202FE2E` | `fat_ioctl` | **22-case** FS_IOCTL dispatcher (lfn buffers, dir info, seek) | high |
93	| `0x0202EC6A` | `fat_fsel` | file-select dispatcher: first/next/prev/num/path + cycle modes — the patch/bank browser primitive | high |
94	| `0x0202B96C` | `exfat_build_entry_set` | build 0x85/0xC0/0xC1 entries + name hash | high |
95	| `0x0202B7C8` / `0x0202B7F2` / `0x0202B8EA` | exfat entry-set checksum / verify / write | rotate-add checksum skipping bytes 2-3 | high/med |
96	| `0x0202B53A` … `0x0202BCF2` | FAT name/LFN helpers | 8.3 convert `0x0202B5E6`, LFN create `0x0202BCDE`, shortname checksum `0x0202BCBE` | high |
97	
98	---
99	
100	## 3. VM flash key-value store (syscfg backend)
101	
102	JieLi's EEPROM-emulation "VM" layer: a ping-pong pair of flash sectors holding
103	append-only records, ids 0..255.
104	
105	- **`vm_area_init` `0x02032140`**: gets the area from `norflash_ioctl(206)`; region
106	  size ≤ 8 kB or 16 kB by type; splits it in half — two sector bases at
107	  `[0x1C0E670+9252]` and `+9264`, half-size at `+9256`; **512-byte record offset cache**
108	  at `0x1C0E670+9276` (256 halfwords, one per id, `0x02032226..0x0203223C`);
109	  then `vm_mount_scan` `0x02027858`.
110	- **Sector magics**: first word of a sector is **`0x55AAAA54`** when freshly
111	  formatted/active and **`0xDDEEAA54`** for the retiring side
112	  (`0x02032294..0x020322AC`; written by `vm_sector_format` `0x0202707C`, swapped by
113	  `vm_garbage_collect` `0x02027112`, maintenance entry `vm_maintenance_locked`
114	  `0x02027292`) — conf med.
115	- **`vm_read` `0x0203249C`** (`id`, `buf`, `buflen`): id < 256 (`vm_id_valid`
116	  `0x02032490`); cached record offset `h[0x1C0E670+9276+id*2]`; active sector selected
117	  by state byte bit 1 (`b[0x1C0E670+9874]`); record = **4-byte header** {check byte,
118	  flags, 12-bit length at bits 4..15} + payload; integrity via the hardware CRC unit
119	  (`chip_crc16` `0x020025DA`, SFR `0x13500`), masked compare at `0x02032550`;
120	  errors −508/−510/−512; mutex `0x1C0E670+9788`.
121	- Writes: `vm_chunk_write` `0x02076B7A` (32-byte chunks through the flash device
122	  vtable), `vm_store_cursor_adjust` `0x02076B60`; GC relocates live records and swaps
123	  the ping-pong sector (`0x02027112`).
124	- **syscfg sits on top**: `syscfg_read` `0x02002612` / `syscfg_write` `0x020032B8`
125	  dispatch config items through a registered ops table (SYS, high).
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 4. DX7 patch storage
130	
131	- The live edit buffer is the 155-byte VCED at **`0x1C0E670+5608`**.
132	- **`dx7voice_pack_store` `0x0201D532`** (high): packs VCED → 128-byte DX7 VMEM on the
133	  stack, then writes it to flash:
134	  - 6 ops × 21 bytes → 6 × 17 bytes with visible bit-packing (rates/levels merged,
135	    `0x0201D562..0x0201D5C8`); loop until 126 input bytes;
136	  - +9 pitch-EG bytes → VMEM+102; packed byte at +111; 4 LFO bytes at +112; packed
137	    sync/feedback byte at +116; +1 at +117; 10-byte name at +118 (total 128);
138	  - store address = `[0x1C0E670+256]` (bank base, set from board config) +
139	    `b[0x1C0E670+4778] << 7` (voice slot × 128), via `norflash_read` `0x02003712`
140	    (read-modify) + `norflash_write` `0x020037B4`, 128 bytes;
141	  - marker `b[0x1C0E670+5763] = 63` set first.
142	- The bank save UI is the menu page with string **`'  Dx7 32 Voice Save To ...  '`**
143	  `0x0204F3AE` — 32 voices × 128 B = one 4 kB sector per bank, matching the 0x20
144	  sector-erase granularity (med).
145	- Loading: `dx7patch_select_apply` `0x0201DAB8` — select patch: load, unpack, apply
146	  params, show name.
147	
148	---
149	
150	## 5. Firmware update (ufw / jlfs / OTA)
151	
152	- **`jieli_ufw_update_run` `0x02082D24`**: allocates a 580-byte context
153	  (`mspace_malloc` `0x0205672E`), 1024-byte block buffer; checks the file-type magic
154	  (compares against **`0x5A04` / `0x5A08`** at `0x02082D84..0x02082D98`);
155	  `jieli_update_dispatch` `0x02083394` covers types **`0x5A02..0x5A08`**;
156	  `jieli_update_file_check` `0x0208332A` deletes or format-and-hangs on mismatch;
157	  progress callback through `[0x1C0E670+608]`.
158	- Package entries located from a 3-entry × 32-byte name table at `0x0204E4A4`
159	  (`0x02082DAC..0x02082DEE`), each name decrypted with **`jl_sfc_cipher` `0x020824FA`**
160	  (XOR stream, `key ^ (offset>>2)` per 32-byte block) and CRC-checked
161	  (`cfg_header_crc_check` `0x02026F8E`).
162	- Update file names (rodata `0x02082365..`): `Zedr_ota2.bin`, `Zsd_update2.bin`,
163	  `Zble_app_ota.bin`, `Zspp_app_ota.bin`, `Zusb_update2.bin`, `Zble_ota.bin`,
164	  `Zuart_user.bin`, `Znor_ota.bin`, `Znet_ota.bin`, `Zusb_hid_ota.bin` `0x02082419`,
165	  `ota.bin` `0x0208243A`; `LOADER.BIN` `0x02055831`.
166	- **jlfs** (JieLi library FS) package verify: `jlfs_entry_find_load` `0x020829F2` —
167	  find 32-byte entry by name, decrypt + CRC-verify payload; reader context
168	  `update_ctx_alloc` `0x020824AE` (104 B), `update_state_notify` `0x020824DE`.
169	- **OTA/update callback**: `update_state_callback` `0x02027EE2` — builds a 15-byte
170	  status record (leading bytes `89,48,8` …, one's-complement checksum tail) into
171	  `0x1C0E810+396`, posts `sys_event`, and resets on completion; the update-mode device
172	  path comes from `update_file_open` `0x02028998` (opens on the `'usb_update_mode'`
173	  `0x02055762` device, verifies entry CRCs). Firmware id string **`'FM-1_009'`**
174	  `0x0204F241`; ufw magic fragment `'"3DUfw'` `0x0204EF3E`.
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 6. Recovered storage interfaces
179	
180	- `vm_read 0x0203249C(id, buffer, length)` returns a stored record length or a
181	  negative status. `vm_id_valid 0x02032490` restricts IDs to values below 256.
182	- `vm_chunk_write 0x02076B7A` appends a four-byte-header record while holding
183	  the VM mutex at `ENG+9788`; `syscfg_write 0x020032B8` dispatches through the
184	  higher-level configuration backends.
185	- `norflash_write 0x020038A2` reaches the low-level write path, while erase
186	  operations use 4 KiB granularity. `norflash_write_core 0x0200380A` applies
187	  transformation rules around the encrypted-region boundary stored at
188	  `[0x01C20190+36]`.
189	- `fatfs_fopen 0x0202CA26`, `norfs_fopen 0x020286A0`, and
190	  `fat_fsel 0x0202EC6A` expose the file and directory operations used by the
191	  application.
192	
193	These are internal stock-firmware entry points, not stable APIs. In particular,
194	the inferred free regions and encryption boundary have not been validated as
195	safe targets for external writes.

the firmware XIP image, a small NOR-resident file area ("sdfile"/norfs), a FAT/exFAT
volume, the VM (virtual-memory EEPROM-emulation) key-value area used by syscfg, and the
raw DX7 bank/patch region. Confidence: **high** = proven, **med** = strong inference,
**low** = guess.

Primary evidence: `analysis/shards/shard_020847aa_020847f2.txt`,
`shard_02084824_0208c3b4.txt` (SPI0/flash low level),
`shard_02002154_02003b52.txt` (ROM-call read/write cores),
`shard_02027346_02028fc6.txt` (flash ioctl, device framework, update file open),
`shard_02028fd2_0202b3d6.txt` + `shard_0202b498_0202e0fa.txt` + `shard_0202e108_0203091c.txt`
(FAT/VFS), `shard_02030942_02033964.txt` (VM KV), `shard_02019e9e_0201f07e.txt`
(DX7 pack/store), `shard_02082d14_0208478a.txt` (ufw/jlfs).

---

## 1. NOR flash driver (SPI0)

**SPI0 base `0x11C00`** (jielie `spi.md`: CON+0, BUF+8; CON bit15 PND, bit14 PCLR).
Low-level (all high conf):

| addr | name | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `0x020847AA` | `spi0_wait_ok` | poll `[0x11C00]` sign bit (PND) with 50 000 000-iteration timeout, clear via `\|= 0x4000`; returns 0 ok / −1 timeout |
| `0x020847DA` | `spi0_send_byte` | set TX direction (`\|= 8`, clear bit 12), `[0x11C00+8] = byte`, wait, restore |
| `0x0208478A` | `norflash_cs` | CS low/high helper (r0 = 0/1) |
| `0x02084700` | `norflash_spi0_guard` | wait SFC idle, save/restore SPI0 CON around bit-banged phases |
| `0x020847F2` | `norflash_enter_4byte_addr` | if flash size `[0x1C20190+24] > 16 MB` and addr ≥ 16 MB: one-shot **EN4B `0xB7`** |

**Command-mode engine `norflash_cs_and_erase` `0x02084BBE`** (med): enters SFC command
mode via SFR **`0x40200`** — saves `[0x1C20190+56]`, programs SPI0 CON from

command. The merged cluster around it contains:

- **page program**: WREN (`0x02084824` + verify `0x02084862`), opcode `0x02`,
  3/4-byte address via `spiflash_send_addr` `0x02084872`, byte loop, wait-ready
  `0x020848D0`, icache sync `0x02084B88` — at `0x02084C24`;
- **read**: dispatch `spiflash_io_dispatch` `0x02084A30` (single/dual/quad by chip type);
- **erase** at `0x02084D4E`: selector − 200 → `tbb` table —
  4 kB sector (`0x20`), 64 kB block (`0xD8`), whole chip (`0xC7`), 256-byte page
  (`0x81`, **med**); bounds-checked against `[0x1C20190+24]` flash size;
- **JEDEC ID** `0x9F` → 3 bytes into `[0x1C20190+28]`; **unique ID** `0x4B`
  (4 dummy + 16 UID bytes) — at `0x02084CC6`.

**Normal (memory-mapped) data path** — the CPU reads flash XIP, writes/erases go
through mask-ROM services (high):

| addr | name | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `0x0200372C` | `norflash_read_core` | mutex `0x1C0E670+2196` (`os_mutex_pend` `0x0205AE98`), bounds vs `[0x1C20190+24]`, reads in ≤256 B chunks via ROM **`0xFFC00404`** |
| `0x020037B4` | `norflash_read` | public wrapper, returns 0 on short read |
| `0x0200380A` | `norflash_write_core` | ROM **`0xFFC00476`**; then re-scrambles any data in the encrypted region (`< [0x1C20190+36]`) with the boot key `h[0x1C7FD50+28]` via the LFSR cipher `0x020037C8` |
| `0x020038A2` | `norflash_write` | public wrapper, 0 on failure |
| `0x02001D33A` | `norflash_ioctl` | device ioctl: erase/write/cache-control commands, mutex-guarded (cmd 206 = query VM area, used by `vm_area_init`) |
| `0x02028BA2` | `norflash_dev_init` | JEDEC read, capacity = 2^n, registers the device into the framework |

---

## 2. Filesystems

Two stacks share the flash through the device framework (devices `'norflash'`
`0x02055780`, `'nor_sdfile'` `0x0205572D`, `'sdfile_fat'` `0x02055738`, `'ramfs'`
`0x0204EAEC`, `'virtual'` `0x0204EC40`).

### 2.1 norfs — the "sdfile" NOR area (med)

A tiny JieLi filesystem of **CRC'd 32-byte directory entries** directly on NOR flash:

- `norfs_fopen` `0x020286A0` — resolve path → 40 B file object (`norfs_file_obj_init`
  `0x02028220`), trailing read/write/seek/close ops;
- `norfs_path_find` `0x0202852C`, `norfs_dir_find_entry` `0x020283D0`,
  `norfs_entry_scan` `0x0202847A` (≤32 entries, crc16 + name match),
  `norfs_addr_remap` `0x020283B4`;
- FM-1 content: `mnt/sdfile/app/usr` `0x0204F0A1`, `mnt/sdfile/app/btif` `0x0204F12E`,
  `mnt/sdfile/app/cfg_tool.bin` `0x0204F33C`, `res.bin` `0x0204EC48` (UI resources,
  read through `ui_res_read` `0x020100CE` with read-ahead cache).

### 2.2 FAT12/16/32 + exFAT (FatFS-derived, extended)

| addr | name | notes | conf |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x02029352` | `mount_volume` | parse BPB; exFAT detected via OEM field at +67 (`u32` + `'T'` byte check, `0x02029374..0x0202939C`); FAT12/16/32 by cluster count | high |
| `0x02029210` | `mount_alloc_fs` | allocate + link FATFS object, query sector count | med |
| `0x0202AEF8` | `fatfs_obj_alloc` | 812-byte filesystem work object | low |
| `0x020292FC` | `move_window` | sync then load sector into the FAT window | high |
| `0x0202C19A` | `fatfs_open` | open/create by path, truncate + exFAT handling | med |
| `0x0202CA26` | `fatfs_fopen` | mode-string (`r`/`w`/`rb`) front-end | med |
| `0x02029762` | `f_mkfs` | format: pick geometry, write BPB/FAT/root | high |
| `0x0202E1E2` | `fat_dir_walk` | recursive walk: attr filter, wildcard, callback, path stack | med |
| `0x0202FE2E` | `fat_ioctl` | **22-case** FS_IOCTL dispatcher (lfn buffers, dir info, seek) | high |
| `0x0202EC6A` | `fat_fsel` | file-select dispatcher: first/next/prev/num/path + cycle modes — the patch/bank browser primitive | high |
| `0x0202B96C` | `exfat_build_entry_set` | build 0x85/0xC0/0xC1 entries + name hash | high |
| `0x0202B7C8` / `0x0202B7F2` / `0x0202B8EA` | exfat entry-set checksum / verify / write | rotate-add checksum skipping bytes 2-3 | high/med |
| `0x0202B53A` … `0x0202BCF2` | FAT name/LFN helpers | 8.3 convert `0x0202B5E6`, LFN create `0x0202BCDE`, shortname checksum `0x0202BCBE` | high |

---

## 3. VM flash key-value store (syscfg backend)

JieLi's EEPROM-emulation "VM" layer: a ping-pong pair of flash sectors holding
append-only records, ids 0..255.

- **`vm_area_init` `0x02032140`**: gets the area from `norflash_ioctl(206)`; region
  size ≤ 8 kB or 16 kB by type; splits it in half — two sector bases at
  `[0x1C0E670+9252]` and `+9264`, half-size at `+9256`; **512-byte record offset cache**
  at `0x1C0E670+9276` (256 halfwords, one per id, `0x02032226..0x0203223C`);
  then `vm_mount_scan` `0x02027858`.
- **Sector magics**: first word of a sector is **`0x55AAAA54`** when freshly
  formatted/active and **`0xDDEEAA54`** for the retiring side
  (`0x02032294..0x020322AC`; written by `vm_sector_format` `0x0202707C`, swapped by
  `vm_garbage_collect` `0x02027112`, maintenance entry `vm_maintenance_locked`
  `0x02027292`) — conf med.
- **`vm_read` `0x0203249C`** (`id`, `buf`, `buflen`): id < 256 (`vm_id_valid`
  `0x02032490`); cached record offset `h[0x1C0E670+9276+id*2]`; active sector selected
  by state byte bit 1 (`b[0x1C0E670+9874]`); record = **4-byte header** {check byte,
  flags, 12-bit length at bits 4..15} + payload; integrity via the hardware CRC unit
  (`chip_crc16` `0x020025DA`, SFR `0x13500`), masked compare at `0x02032550`;
  errors −508/−510/−512; mutex `0x1C0E670+9788`.
- Writes: `vm_chunk_write` `0x02076B7A` (32-byte chunks through the flash device
  vtable), `vm_store_cursor_adjust` `0x02076B60`; GC relocates live records and swaps
  the ping-pong sector (`0x02027112`).
- **syscfg sits on top**: `syscfg_read` `0x02002612` / `syscfg_write` `0x020032B8`
  dispatch config items through a registered ops table (SYS, high).

---

## 4. DX7 patch storage

- The live edit buffer is the 155-byte VCED at **`0x1C0E670+5608`**.
- **`dx7voice_pack_store` `0x0201D532`** (high): packs VCED → 128-byte DX7 VMEM on the
  stack, then writes it to flash:
  - 6 ops × 21 bytes → 6 × 17 bytes with visible bit-packing (rates/levels merged,
    `0x0201D562..0x0201D5C8`); loop until 126 input bytes;
  - +9 pitch-EG bytes → VMEM+102; packed byte at +111; 4 LFO bytes at +112; packed
    sync/feedback byte at +116; +1 at +117; 10-byte name at +118 (total 128);
  - store address = `[0x1C0E670+256]` (bank base, set from board config) +
    `b[0x1C0E670+4778] << 7` (voice slot × 128), via `norflash_read` `0x02003712`
    (read-modify) + `norflash_write` `0x020037B4`, 128 bytes;
  - marker `b[0x1C0E670+5763] = 63` set first.
- The bank save UI is the menu page with string **`'  Dx7 32 Voice Save To ...  '`**
  `0x0204F3AE` — 32 voices × 128 B = one 4 kB sector per bank, matching the 0x20
  sector-erase granularity (med).
- Loading: `dx7patch_select_apply` `0x0201DAB8` — select patch: load, unpack, apply
  params, show name.

---

## 5. Firmware update (ufw / jlfs / OTA)

- **`jieli_ufw_update_run` `0x02082D24`**: allocates a 580-byte context
  (`mspace_malloc` `0x0205672E`), 1024-byte block buffer; checks the file-type magic
  (compares against **`0x5A04` / `0x5A08`** at `0x02082D84..0x02082D98`);
  `jieli_update_dispatch` `0x02083394` covers types **`0x5A02..0x5A08`**;
  `jieli_update_file_check` `0x0208332A` deletes or format-and-hangs on mismatch;
  progress callback through `[0x1C0E670+608]`.
- Package entries located from a 3-entry × 32-byte name table at `0x0204E4A4`
  (`0x02082DAC..0x02082DEE`), each name decrypted with **`jl_sfc_cipher` `0x020824FA`**
  (XOR stream, `key ^ (offset>>2)` per 32-byte block) and CRC-checked
  (`cfg_header_crc_check` `0x02026F8E`).
- Update file names (rodata `0x02082365..`): `Zedr_ota2.bin`, `Zsd_update2.bin`,
  `Zble_app_ota.bin`, `Zspp_app_ota.bin`, `Zusb_update2.bin`, `Zble_ota.bin`,
  `Zuart_user.bin`, `Znor_ota.bin`, `Znet_ota.bin`, `Zusb_hid_ota.bin` `0x02082419`,
  `ota.bin` `0x0208243A`; `LOADER.BIN` `0x02055831`.
- **jlfs** (JieLi library FS) package verify: `jlfs_entry_find_load` `0x020829F2` —
  find 32-byte entry by name, decrypt + CRC-verify payload; reader context
  `update_ctx_alloc` `0x020824AE` (104 B), `update_state_notify` `0x020824DE`.
- **OTA/update callback**: `update_state_callback` `0x02027EE2` — builds a 15-byte
  status record (leading bytes `89,48,8` …, one's-complement checksum tail) into
  `0x1C0E810+396`, posts `sys_event`, and resets on completion; the update-mode device
  path comes from `update_file_open` `0x02028998` (opens on the `'usb_update_mode'`
  `0x02055762` device, verifies entry CRCs). Firmware id string **`'FM-1_009'`**
  `0x0204F241`; ufw magic fragment `'"3DUfw'` `0x0204EF3E`.

---

## 6. Recovered storage interfaces

- `vm_read 0x0203249C(id, buffer, length)` returns a stored record length or a
  negative status. `vm_id_valid 0x02032490` restricts IDs to values below 256.
- `vm_chunk_write 0x02076B7A` appends a four-byte-header record while holding
  the VM mutex at `ENG+9788`; `syscfg_write 0x020032B8` dispatches through the
  higher-level configuration backends.
- `norflash_write 0x020038A2` reaches the low-level write path, while erase
  operations use 4 KiB granularity. `norflash_write_core 0x0200380A` applies
  transformation rules around the encrypted-region boundary stored at
  `[0x01C20190+36]`.
- `fatfs_fopen 0x0202CA26`, `norfs_fopen 0x020286A0`, and
  `fat_fsel 0x0202EC6A` expose the file and directory operations used by the
  application.

These are internal stock-firmware entry points, not stable APIs. In particular,
the inferred free regions and encryption boundary have not been validated as
safe targets for external writes.

export GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1; git switch -c m7/start && cat >> docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md <<'EOF'

### SR-9: Flash storage: the region firmware may use, the part, and code while the flash is busy
- Asked: 2026-10-24, session M7 (firmware side)
- Question: (a) On an FM-1, which flash chip offsets our firmware may use
  for its own data without harming the boot chain or the update path:
  what lies below `0x4000`, whether anything past an installed image
  (the chip's last sectors, say) is used by the boot chain or the update
  path, and the chip's size on the FM-1. (b) The FM-1's flash part, and
  from its datasheet: the 4 KiB erase's and the page program's times
  (typical and maximum), the endurance (erase cycles a sector), and
  whether it can suspend an erase or program. (c) On the chip, while an
  erase or a program is in progress: what reads through the code window
  do (wait until it ends, read wrong data, fault), for core 1 too.
  (d) On the chip: whether firmware may drive SPI0 with HW-47's commands
  while the code window is in use, or what must be idle or set up first
  (SPI0's clock and mode on the chip, the code window's own controller),
  and how the window is restored after. (e) Whether the code window
  caches the flash on the chip, and what makes it see a change made
  through SPI0. (f) Whether the chip starts with any write protection set
  (the status register's protect bits) that must be cleared before an
  erase or program. (g) In fwtest: SPI0's pace (emulated time per byte),
  what a page program does to bytes that are not erased (clears bits
  only, or overwrites), and to an address range past the end of a
  256-byte page (wraps within the page, or not).
- Why: M7 is flash storage: user patches, the patch selection and the
  settings, written so a power cut at any instant keeps the previous good
  copy, and so saving never makes the audio underrun. Without (a) the
  store sits in the chip's last 64 KiB as an assumption, in one define,
  and the image is kept clear of it. Without (c) to (e) the firmware runs
  every instruction and reads every constant from RAM after start-up, and
  reads its store through SPI0 only, so nothing touches the code window
  while the flash may be busy; (c) says whether that is needed. (b) sets
  the write limits each record kind gets, and the busy time the audio
  tests must survive; (f) and (g) decide whether the driver works on the
  chip and in fwtest alike. Read: HARDWARE-SPEC.md HW-5 and HW-47 (both
  emulator-only or preliminary, "M7 should confirm the chip and its
  timing"), the vendored SDK's `WL82.h` (`JL_SPI0`'s registers, no bits
  beyond HW-47's); HARNESS.md ("The raw image", `--flash`,
  `--flash-out`). Black-box runs in fwtest so far: none beyond a
  `--flash-out` capture of an erased chip.
- Status: open
EOF
tail -3 docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md
